  • Features
  • Examples

Welcome to Accessible HTML5

This is a well-structured, accessible HTML5 document demonstrating modern best practices for semantic markup and inclusive design.

It uses semantic landmarks, a skip link for keyboard navigation, and CSS that adapts to your light or dark mode preference.

Text and link colors meet WCAG AA contrast in both themes, type scales with your browser's font size, and motion respects your system settings.

Features

  • Semantic HTML structure with proper landmarks
  • Keyboard accessible navigation and focus management
  • Dark mode support with custom color schemes
  • Responsive typography using modern CSS
  • Print-friendly styles for better readability
  • WCAG AA contrast compliance in all color modes

Examples

Component Cards

Card components are useful for organizing related content. They include a subtle border and padding for visual separation.

Learn more about accessibility resources

Interactive Elements

Buttons and links are fully accessible with clear focus states. All interactive elements include visible focus indicators and proper ARIA labels.

Keyboard navigation: Use Tab to move forward, Shift+Tab to move backward, and Enter or Space to activate.

Accessible Form

Contact Information
For example, name@example.com
Up to 2,000 characters. 2,000 remaining.

Live Region Example

Click the button to announce a message using a live region. This demonstrates how screen readers are notified of dynamic updates.

Interactive Counter

This counter demonstrates state management and ARIA live regions for accessible dynamic content.

Accessible tables have proper headers, captions, and semantic structure for screen readers.

Welcome to Accessible HTML5

This is a well-structured, accessible HTML5 document demonstrating modern best practices for semantic markup and inclusive design.

It uses semantic landmarks, a skip link for keyboard navigation, and CSS that adapts to your light or dark mode preference.

Text and link colors meet WCAG AA contrast in both themes, type scales with your browser's font size, and motion respects your system settings.

Features

  • Semantic HTML structure with proper landmarks
  • Keyboard accessible navigation and focus management
  • Dark mode support with custom color schemes
  • Responsive typography using modern CSS
  • Print-friendly styles for better readability
  • WCAG AA contrast compliance in all color modes

Examples

Component Cards

Card components are useful for organizing related content. They include a subtle border and padding for visual separation.

Buttons and links are fully accessible with clear focus states. All interactive elements include visible focus indicators and proper ARIA labels.

content.text:
I made nine targeted fixes to `0.html`, but none of them have been tested: the syntax and ID-reference checks I tried to run were blocked by the session's permissions, and nothing was opened in a browser. I re-read the edited sections and they look correct.

The file was already in good shape, so these are fixes to specific problems rather than a redesign.

## Accessibility fixes
- **Message field description:** screen readers would have read "remaining" twice, because `aria-describedby` pointed at both the hint and a span inside that hint. It now points at the hint only.
- **Character limit:** screen reader users had no warning as they approached the 2,000-character limit. A visually hidden status region now announces the remaining count when it crosses 100, 50, 25, 10 and 0.
- **Form status:** `role="status"` was combined with `aria-live="assertive"`, which contradict each other. I removed the override, so it is now polite and no longer interrupts the focus announcement when focus moves to the email field.
- **Required marker:** the unexplained `*` on the email label is now a visible "(required)". It stays hidden from screen readers, since the `required` attribute already announces it.

## Behaviour
- **Theme sync across tabs:** changing the theme in one tab now updates other open tabs through a `storage` listener.

## CSS cleanup
- **Legend:** removed the `form-hint` class and the `legend.form-hint` rule that existed only to override it. The rendering should be identical.
- **Dead rule:** removed a forced-colors block that set the focus outline to 3px, which it already was.
- **Logical properties:** list padding and the skip link's position and corner radius now use logical properties, matching the rest of the stylesheet.

## Left alone
- **Placeholder URLs:** the canonical link (`https://www.example.com`) and the GitHub footer link (`https://github.com`) are still placeholders; swap in the real URLs when you have them.
- **Duplicated dark palette:** the dark colours are defined twice. `light-dark()` would remove the duplication, but browsers without support would lose their colours entirely, so I kept it as is.
